```{r}
library(hBayesDM)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r}
full.data <- "full_data.txt"
B1.data <- "env1.txt"
B2.data <- "env2.txt"
B3.data <- "env3.txt"
B4.data <- "env4.txt"
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
```{r}
model3.full <- banditNarm_lapse(data = full.data, niter = 4000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 4, ncore = 4)
saveRDS(model3.full, file = "model3.full.rds")

model3.B1 <- banditNarm_lapse(data = B1.data, niter = 4000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 4, ncore = 4)
saveRDS(model3.B1, file = "model3.B1.rds")

model3.B2 <- banditNarm_lapse(data = B2.data, niter = 4000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 4, ncore = 4)
saveRDS(model3.B2, file = "model3.B2.rds")

model3.B3 <- banditNarm_lapse(data = B3.data, niter = 4000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 4, ncore = 4)
saveRDS(model3.B3, file = "model3.B3.rds")

model3.B4 <- banditNarm_lapse(data = B4.data, niter = 4000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 4, ncore = 4)
saveRDS(model3.B4, file = "model3.B4.rds")
```
```{r}
rhat_full = rhat(model3.full)
write.csv(rhat_full, "rhat_full.csv", row.names = TRUE)
```
```{r}
rhat_4 = rhat(model3.B4)
write.csv(rhat_4, "rhat_B4.csv", row.names = TRUE)
```


```{r}
write.csv(model3.B4$allIndPars, "individual_parameters_B4.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```


```{r}
plot(model3.B4, type = "trace")
```
```{r}
write.csv(model3.B4$parVals, "posterior_distribution_B4.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```


```{r}
waic1 = printFit(model3.full, model3.B1, model3.B2, model3.B3, model3.B4, ic="waic")
write.csv(waic1, "waic.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(bayesplot)

library(gridExtra)  # for arranging multiple plots

# Extract posterior samples from the model
draws <- as.data.frame(model3.B4$parVals)

# List of parameters you want to plot
params_to_plot <- c("mu_Arew", "mu_Apun", "mu_R", "mu_P", "mu_xi")

plot_list <- lapply(params_to_plot, function(param) {
  mcmc_areas(draws, pars = param) + ggtitle(paste("Posterior of", param))
})

# Arrange plots in a grid
grid.arrange(grobs = plot_list, ncol = 2)

```
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)

# Read the CSV files
b1_data <- "individual_parameters_B1.csv"
b2_data <- "individual_parameters_B2.csv" 
b3_data <- "individual_parameters_B3.csv"
b4_data <- "individual_parameters_B4.csv"
# Extract punishment learning rates (Apun)
# B1: fast vol, high stoch
# B2: slow vol high stoch
# B3: fast vol low stoch
# B4: slow vol low stoch

# Calculate means and standard errors
b1_mean <- mean(b1_data$Apun)
b1_se <- sd(b1_data$Apun) / sqrt(nrow(b1_data))

b2_mean <- mean(b2_data$Apun)
b2_se <- sd(b2_data$Apun) / sqrt(nrow(b2_data))

b3_mean <- mean(b3_data$Apun)
b3_se <- sd(b3_data$Apun) / sqrt(nrow(b3_data))

b4_mean <- mean(b4_data$Apun)
b4_se <- sd(b4_data$Apun) / sqrt(nrow(b4_data))

# Create a data frame for plotting
plot_data <- data.frame(
  Stochasticity = factor(c("High", "High", "Low", "Low"), levels = c("Low", "High")),
  Volatility = factor(c("Fast", "Slow", "Fast", "Slow"), levels = c("Slow", "Fast")),
  Mean = c(b1_mean, b2_mean, b3_mean, b4_mean),
  SE = c(b1_se, b2_se, b3_se, b4_se)
)

# Generate colors based on stochasticity level
get_color <- function(stoch_level) {
  if (stoch_level == "Low") {
    return("steelblue")
  } else {
    return("lightblue")
  }
}

plot_data$Color <- sapply(as.character(plot_data$Stochasticity), get_color)

# Create the plot
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Stochasticity, y = Mean, color = Stochasticity)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = Volatility), size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = Mean - SE, ymax = Mean + SE, linetype = Volatility),
    width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Low" = "steelblue", "High" = "lightblue")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Slow" = "dashed", "Fast" = "solid")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Slow" = 16, "Fast" = 16)) +  # Both use circle shape
  labs(y = "Punishment Learning Rate (Apun)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    text = element_text(size = 12)
  )

# Print summary statistics
print(plot_data)
```
